title: A clinical de-identification model lost accuracy on intensive-care notes
summary: EdgeDeID, trained on synthetic notes, scored 0.478 F1 on 2,434 MIMIC intensive-care nursing notes, compared with 0.994 on 100 synthetic notes. A separately trained clinical text model scored 0.675 on the intensive-care set. The test corpora differ in writing style and annotation conventions.
organization: Sharif University of Technology; Mayo Clinic; Yale University

source_review.scope: v1 §4.1 and Table 4 external clinical-text evaluation

evidence.tested: External notes use replaced identifiers and human labels. The paper also reports an analysis limited to the 823 Safe Harbor spans.
evidence.unknown: The evaluation does not establish safe redaction or portability. Style and label differences both affect the synthetic-to-clinical comparison.
evidence.ai_role: Fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B detects surrogate identifiers in clinical notes.
